en: to be passed; to be handed

examples.en: I was handed a present by my friend.
I took the receipt from the clerk and went out.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 주는 음식은 건네받지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't accept food handed to you by a stranger.

examples.ko: 열쇠를 건네받는 순간 이사 온 실감이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I was handed the key, it felt real that I had moved in.
The student who was handed the microphone sang a song.
When you are handed the documents, please check them right away.

explain: '건네주다'의 반대로, 받는 사람 입장에서 말해요. '받다'보다 상대가 손으로 직접 내밀어 준 느낌이 있어요. 'A에게서 B를 건네받다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I took the key that was handed to me and went inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 다음에 다른 일을 이어서 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link another action after receiving.

phrases.en: I was handed the documents by a staff member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 물건을 손으로 직접 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you receive papers or items directly by hand.

phrases.en: I handed a book to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요. 받는 사람이면 '건네받다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the giver's side; the receiver uses 건네받다.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '건네주다' and is said from the receiver's point of view. Compared with '받다', it feels like the other person held it out and handed it over. It is used like 'A에게서 B를 건네받다'.

en: in a flash; (forget) for a moment

examples.en: I completely forgot where I put my key.
I forgot the appointment time.
The light flickered on and then went off again.
The train left in the blink of an eye.
I dozed off for a second while driving, and it was really scary.

examples.ko: 숙제를 깜박한 학생은 손을 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Students who forgot their homework, please raise your hand.

explain: '깜박 잊다', '깜박 졸다'처럼 정신이 잠깐 나가는 느낌이에요. '깜빡'도 같은 말이에요. '깜박했어요'는 잊어버린 걸 가볍게 말해서 친구에게 사과할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Sorry, I forgot for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜박'과 같은 말이에요. 요즘은 '깜빡'을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word as 깜박; 깜빡 is more common nowadays.

phrases.en: I forgot to bring my umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 일을 잠깐 잊었을 때 가볍게 말해요. 사과할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to say you forgot something; fits when apologizing.

phrases.example: 버스에서 깜박 졸다가 내릴 곳을 지나쳤어요.
phrases.en: I dozed off for a moment on the bus and missed my stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 짧은 시간 잠깐 잠드는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means falling asleep for just a very short time.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of your mind slipping away for a moment, as in '깜박 잊다' or '깜박 졸다'. '깜빡' is the same word. '깜박했어요' makes forgetting sound light, so it fits an apology to a friend.

examples.ko: 줄 끄트머리에 서 있는 사람이 제 친구예요.
examples.en: The person standing at the very end of the line is my friend.
The ends of my hair were split, so I cut them.
There is a small bakery at the far end of the alley.

examples.ko: 실 끄트머리를 잡고 천천히 당겨 보세요.
examples.en: Hold the end of the thread and pull slowly.
The culprit was only revealed at the very end of the story.
It's the tail end of winter, so the wind is still cold.

explain: '끝'보다 맨 끝쪽의 작은 부분을 가리키는 느낌이에요. 물건의 끝뿐 아니라 길, 이야기, 계절처럼 시간이나 공간의 끝부분에도 써요. 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이고 '끝자락'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 줄 끄트머리에 서 있는 사람이 제 친구예요.
phrases.en: The person standing at the very end of the line is my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이나 길의 맨 끝쪽 자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the very end of a line or road.
phrases.en_equiv: to stand at the tail end

phrases.en: It's the tail end of summer, so mornings and evenings are cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끄트머리'와 비슷하고, 계절이나 시간의 끝부분에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '끄트머리', and fits well with the end of a season or period of time.

phrases.en: My hair ends were split, so I cut them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이나 실처럼 가늘고 긴 것의 끝이 갈라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the end of something thin and long, like hair or thread, splits.

explain_en: It points to the small part at the very tip, a bit more specific than '끝'. It is used not only for the end of an object but also for the end part of a road, a story, or a season. It is a casual word and is sometimes used like '끝자락'.

examples.ko: 화가 난 형이 가방을 바닥에 내동댕이쳤어요.
examples.en: My angry older brother flung his bag onto the floor.
The child hurls the toy into the corner of the room.
If you fling things like that, they'll break.
He tossed aside his long-held plan overnight.
Even if you're angry, please don't throw your phone down.

examples.ko: 동생이 신발을 현관에 내동댕이쳐 놓고 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling flung their shoes down in the entryway and left.

explain: '던지다'보다 홱 거칠게 던지는 느낌이고, 화가 났거나 물건을 함부로 다룰 때 잘 어울려요. 계획이나 책임을 아무렇게나 버린다는 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 화가 나서 모자를 땅에 내동댕이쳤어요.
phrases.en: He was angry and threw his hat onto the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로 이미 거칠게 던진 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form, describing a rough throw that already happened.

phrases.en: Please don't fling the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 물건을 함부로 다루지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command telling someone not to handle things carelessly.

phrases.en: The child flings the doll onto the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바닥에'와 함께 쓰면 던져서 떨어지는 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '바닥에' the picture of it being thrown down is clear.

explain_en: It is rougher than '던지다', a sudden rough fling, and fits when someone is angry or careless with things. It is also used figuratively for casually discarding a plan or responsibility.

en: to let go; to set free

examples.en: I let the fish I caught go again.
I set the bird free to fly away.
Please, let that person go now.
When I let the cat go, it ran away immediately.

examples.ko: 아이 손을 놔주면 길을 잃을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you let go of the child's hand, they could get lost.
I still haven't been able to let go of my old lover.

explain: '놓아주다'의 줄임말이라서 말할 때 훨씬 많이 써요. '놔줘요', '놔줬어요'로 활용해요. 마음에서 사람이나 감정을 보내 주는 비유로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I let the fish I caught go.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놔주다'의 원래 형태예요. 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 놔주다; more common in writing and formal speech.

phrases.en: Please let go of my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡고 있는 것을 놓아 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to someone to release their hold.

phrases.en: I want to let that person go now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 감정을 마음에서 보내 준다는 비유로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for letting go of a person or feeling emotionally.

explain_en: It is the contracted form of '놓아주다' and is used much more in speech. It conjugates as '놔줘요' and '놔줬어요'. It is also often used figuratively for letting a person or feeling go emotionally.

examples.en: I was in a hurry, so I just threw on whatever and came out.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 있는 걸로 되는대로 만들어 먹어요.
examples.en: I just cook whatever I can with what's in the fridge.

examples.ko: 계획 없이 되는대로 살면 나중에 후회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you live carelessly without a plan, you may regret it later.

examples.ko: 책을 되는대로 꽂아 두지 말고 정리하세요.
examples.en: Don't just stick the books in anywhere; organize them.

examples.ko: 일단 되는대로 해 보고 안 되면 다시 생각해요.
examples.en: Let's just try it however we can first, and think again if it doesn't work.
I'll contact you as soon as I have time.

explain: '아무렇게나, 대충'이라는 느낌으로 쓸 때와 '가능한 만큼, 가능해지는 대로'라는 뜻으로 쓸 때가 있어요. '시간 되는대로 연락 드릴게요'는 뒤쪽 쓰임이고, 앞뒤 문장을 보면 구별할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I was in a hurry, so I just threw something on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되는대로'의 '대충' 쪽 뜻과 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to the 'carelessly' sense of the headword.

phrases.en: I had no time, so I made something quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자세히 하지 않고 간단히 한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means doing it roughly without much care.

phrases.en: I'll contact you as soon as I have time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가능해지는 대로'라는 뜻으로, 앞에 말이 와서 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means 'as soon as possible', attached after a noun.

explain_en: It can mean 'carelessly, any old way', or 'as much as possible / as soon as it becomes possible'. '시간 되는대로 연락 드릴게요' is the second use, and the surrounding sentence tells you which one is meant.

examples.ko: 지난 시험의 실수를 이번에 만회하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make up for my mistake on the last test this time.
Our team made up the points in the second half.

examples.ko: 늦잠 잔 시간을 만회하려고 빨리 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked fast to make up for the time I lost oversleeping.
Isn't there a way to make up for the loss?
A goal came that made up for the conceded point.

examples.ko: 이번 달 매출로 지난달 적자를 만회해요.
examples.en: We cover last month's deficit with this month's sales.

explain: '회복하다'는 나빠진 몸이나 상태가 원래대로 돌아올 때 쓰고, '만회하다'는 실수·손해·뒤처진 점수를 다시 채울 때 써요. '실수를 만회하다', '점수를 만회하다'처럼 메워야 할 부정적인 것과 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: I will make up for my mistake in the next game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못한 일을 다시 좋게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make up for something done wrong.
phrases.en_equiv: to make up for a mistake

phrases.en: We made up the points in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤처진 점수를 따라잡을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when catching up on lost points.

phrases.example: 한 번 더 만회할 기회를 주세요.
phrases.en: Please give me one more chance to make up for it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수를 바로잡을 기회를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a chance to fix a mistake.
phrases.en_equiv: a chance to make up for it

explain_en: '회복하다' is for a body or condition returning to normal. '만회하다' is for making up a mistake, loss, or deficit in score. It pairs with something negative to fill in, like '실수를 만회하다' or '점수를 만회하다'.

dis.h: make up for lost points or mistakes

p.n: 회복하다 does not fit a score deficit; 만회하다 means winning back a loss.

examples.en: You need to watch your words in front of elders.
Even between friends, watching your words is a must.
You have to watch what you say in front of a child.

examples.ko: 말조심에 신경 쓰다 보니 대화가 어색해졌어요.
examples.en: Because I was careful about what I said, the conversation became awkward.
Watching your words is also a habit.

examples.ko: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다니까 말조심이 필요해요.
examples.en: Daytime words are heard by birds and nighttime words by mice, so you need to watch your words.

explain: 말조심은 '말조심을 하다', '말조심이 필요하다'처럼 쓰는 명사예요. 짧게 '말조심!'이라고 하면 화가 난 경고로 들릴 수 있어요. 점잖게 말할 때는 '말을 가려서 하세요'가 좋아요.

phrases.en: I watch my words in front of my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '말조심'에 '하다'를 붙인 가장 기본 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic use, attaching '하다' to the noun.

phrases.en: You need to watch your words online too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심해서 말해야 하는 상황을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain situations where one must speak carefully.

phrases.en: Please choose your words carefully with customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말조심'보다 점잖고 부드럽게 충고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A politer, softer way to advise than '말조심'.

explain_en: 말조심 is a noun used in patterns like 말조심을 하다 and 말조심이 필요하다. Said bluntly as 말조심!, it can sound like an angry warning. A politer way is 말을 가려서 하세요.

en: to push; to shove; to jostle

examples.en: Someone shoved me from behind.
People pushed each other as they went in.
I shoved the door open with all my strength.

examples.ko: 아이를 밀치면 다칠 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful, because the child can get hurt if you shove him.
He pushed the plate aside and stood up.

examples.ko: 지하철에서 밀치는 사람 때문에 짜증이 났어요.
examples.en: I got annoyed because of a person who kept shoving in the subway.

explain: '밀치다'는 '밀다'보다 갑작스럽고 거칠게 힘을 줄 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 폭력적인 느낌이 있어요. 활용할 때는 '밀치어'가 줄어서 '밀쳐요', '밀쳤어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: Please don't push when you stand in line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 붙어 있는 곳에서 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask people not to shove in crowded places.

phrases.en: That person pushed the door open and went in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 세게 주고 거칠게 들어가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes going in with rough force.

phrases.en: Push the door and go in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀치다'보다 거칠지 않고 일상에서 가장 평범하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less rough than 'milchida' and the plain everyday word.

explain_en: 밀치다 is used when force is applied more suddenly and roughly than with 밀다. Used on a person, it feels violent. When conjugated, 밀치어 contracts to 밀쳐요 and 밀쳤어요.

en: to drop; to let fall into

examples.en: I left out an important part of the instructions.
I dropped my key down the drain and couldn't find it.

examples.ko: 빠트린 게 없는지 짐을 다시 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check your bags again to see if you've forgotten anything.
You must not leave the date out of the report.
I almost dropped my phone into the water.
I ended up leaving one name off the list.

explain: 물건을 물이나 구멍에 떨어뜨릴 때와, 해야 할 것을 빼먹을 때 모두 써요. '빠뜨리다'도 같은 표준어이고, 일상 대화에서 '빼먹다'는 더 편한 말투예요.

phrases.en: I forgot to put an umbrella in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠트리다'와 같은 표준어이고, 둘 다 똑같이 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An equally standard spelling of 빠트리다; both can be used the same way.

phrases.en: I dropped my phone in the water and it broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 물이나 구멍 안으로 떨어질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for an object falling into water or a hole.

phrases.en: I was in a hurry and skipped one homework item.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 것을 놓친다는 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means missing something you should have done, in a more casual everyday tone.
phrases.en_equiv: to skip; to forget to include

explain_en: It is used both for dropping something into water or a hole and for leaving out something you should include. '빠뜨리다' is an equally standard form, and '빼먹다' is a more casual way to say it in daily talk.

examples.en: I insert a picture in the middle of the document.
I added a video to the presentation.
Which button do I press to insert a table?

examples.ko: 문장 사이에 쉼표를 삽입한 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who put the comma between the sentences?
I'll insert the photo later.

examples.ko: 파일 이름 뒤에 날짜를 삽입하고 저장했어요.
examples.en: I added the date after the file name and saved it.

explain: 컴퓨터 문서에서 그림이나 표를 넣을 때 '삽입'이라는 메뉴를 자주 봐요. 물건을 안에 넣을 때는 일상에서 '넣다'를 쓰고, 삽입하다는 문서·기계·글처럼 격식 있는 상황에 어울려요.

phrases.en: The picture was inserted into the document.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삽입하다'의 피동 표현으로, 무엇이 들어갔는지에 초점을 둬요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on what got inserted.

phrases.en: Please insert a table here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서 작업을 부탁할 때 쓰는 정중한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask for something in document work.

phrases.en: I click 'Insert Picture' in the menu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터 메뉴 이름처럼 명사로 짧게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a short noun, like a computer menu item.

explain_en: You often see a menu called '삽입' when adding pictures or tables in a computer document. For everyday objects Koreans say '넣다' (put in); 삽입하다 fits documents, machines, and writing in a more formal setting.

examples.ko: 농장에서는 큰 귤을 선별해서 따로 담아요.
examples.en: The farm sorts out large tangerines and packs them separately.

examples.ko: 이 일은 선별 작업이 가장 힘들어요.
examples.en: The sorting work is the hardest part of this job.
I went through a screening check at the airport.
Without criteria, selection is hard.
The selection process was fair, so there were no complaints.

examples.ko: 여러 사진 중에서 선별을 하는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to select from among many photos.

explain: '선별'은 많은 것 중에서 기준에 맞는 것만 골라내는 거예요. '선택'은 하나를 고르는 느낌이고, '선별'은 여러 개를 가려내는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I took a screening test at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람 중에서 문제가 있는 사람을 가려내는 검사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A test that picks out people with a problem from a large group.

phrases.en: What is the selection standard?
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 골라낼지 정하는 기준을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard that decides what gets picked out.

phrases.example: 오늘은 하루 종일 선별 작업을 했어요.
phrases.en: I did sorting work all day today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일이나 물건을 크기, 품질별로 나누는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sorting fruit or goods by size or quality.

explain_en: 선별 is picking out only the items that meet a standard from a large pool. 선택 feels like choosing one, while 선별 feels like screening out several.

examples.en: Mom keeps urging us to hurry out.

examples.ko: 너무 재촉하지 마세요. 거의 다 했어요.
examples.en: Please do not rush me so much. I am almost done.
The customer kept hurrying the food, so the staff was busy.

examples.ko: 친구가 대답을 재촉하는 바람에 마음이 급했어요.
examples.en: My friend pressed me for an answer, so I felt rushed.
The landlord urged me to pay the rent.
The more you urge a child to hurry, the slower the child gets.

explain: 상대에게 빨리하라고 압박할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 부담스럽게 들릴 수 있어요. 부드럽게 말할 때는 '서둘러 주세요'가 좋아요. '독촉하다'는 돈이나 일을 내라고 계속 요구할 때 주로 써요.

phrases.en: Please don't rush me so much. I'll go soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨리하라고 계속 말하는 상대에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone who keeps pushing you to stop.

phrases.en: My friend keeps telling me to hurry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재촉하다'보다 쉬운 말로 빨리하라고 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say someone urges you to hurry.

phrases.en: The shop owner pressed me to pay the money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 일을 내라고 계속 요구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when repeatedly demanding money or work.

explain_en: It is used when you press someone to be quick, and it can sound a bit pushy. For a softer request, '서둘러 주세요' works better. '독촉하다' is mostly for repeatedly demanding money or work.

p.n: 다그치다 is harsher, pressing for an answer or explanation.

examples.en: The bus came speeding toward me and I was startled.

examples.ko: 늦을 것 같아서 역까지 전속력으로 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I thought I'd be late, so I ran to the station at full speed.

examples.ko: 배가 전속력을 내자 바닷바람이 세게 불었어요.
examples.en: When the ship went to full speed, the sea wind blew hard.

examples.ko: 전속력으로 달리는 기차 안에서 창밖을 봤어요.
examples.en: I looked out the window of the train running at full speed.

examples.ko: 엔진이 전속력에 가까워지면 소리가 아주 커져요.
examples.en: When the engine nears full speed, the noise gets very loud.

examples.ko: 아이가 전속력으로 달려와서 엄마 품에 안겼어요.
examples.en: The child ran at full speed and jumped into her mother's arms.

explain: '전속력으로 달리다', '전속력을 내다'처럼 달리기나 탈것의 속도와 함께 써요. 일이나 노력에는 잘 안 쓰고, 그럴 때는 '최선을 다해서'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The car runs at full speed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.en: I was late, so I went at full speed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속도를 최대한 높일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when raising speed to the maximum.

phrases.en: It rained, so I ran as fast as I could.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아주 빨리 뛰어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person runs very fast.
phrases.en_equiv: to run off at full speed

explain_en: It pairs with movement, as in '전속력으로 달리다' (run at full speed) and '전속력을 내다' (go full speed). It is not used for effort at work or study; there you say '최선을 다해서' (doing one's best).
